scope: Manual three-paper FDP/FDR comparison with paper-qualified null-set and procedure interpretations.

rows.query: Pinned full-Mathlib rg search for false-discovery rate/proportion found no specialized statistical definition; inspected finite indicator sums and Bochner integral, and registered p0078,p0157,p1564 PDF page5 for each source-specific null set and procedure.
rows.result: Finite binary rejection counts, a denominator bounded below by one and expectation under the data law directly express FDP and FDR for all three variants.
rows.gap: The formulas are directly expressible after supplying each paper’s null set and measurable rejection procedure; FDR control remains a separate theorem.

comparisons.aos-2024-v52-i01-p0078/D2: For each graph node j in[d], let psi_j be its binary rejection decision and count false rejections only where the TRUE node degree is strictly less than k_tau. Divide that count by max(1,sum_j psi_j), then integrate under the graphical-model data law. Degree equal to k_tau belongs to the alternative, and the hypothesis family is nodes, not individual edges; retain the graph’s node-set convention in the bipartite and undirected settings. If no node is rejected the numerator is zero and denominator one, so FDP=0 without any undefined division. The displayed numerator’s upper d and H0 notation mean summing over null nodes within[d]. No library ingredient proves StarTrek’s control at level q merely from this definition.
comparisons.aos-2024-v52-i01-p0157/D2: Use the joint law P of all training and test observations and the measurable test-index rejection set R(Z) subset{1,...,m}. The true-null set consists of TEST indices whose marginal P_i equals P0, not the calibration index set or a set determined by estimated density equality. FDP is card(R intersection H0)/max(1,card R), and FDR is its expectation over the full data law, including any dependence and the score-fitting data. Empty R gives exactly zero. Because the random ratio is bounded in[0,1], it is integrable once measurable; do not replace E of this ratio by a ratio of expected counts or a conditional-bootstrap expectation.
comparisons.aos-2024-v52-i04-p1564/D4: At each fixed theta in R^n, let phi_i(X) in{0,1} be the measurable rejection decision, count the decisions at coordinates satisfying theta_i=0, and divide by max(1,sum_i phi_i(X)). Integrate with respect to the data law at that fixed theta; this is a frequentist expectation, not an average over a prior on theta. The null set is parameter-dependent and differs from a graph-degree or distribution-equality null. Empty rejection gives zero and the ratio is bounded, so ordinary probability integration applies. A sequence of procedures may depend on n, but that convention does not change the finite-n definition or imply asymptotic control.
